newsitem.title: FRANCE: French grain prices steady on slow demand.
newsitem.headline: French grain prices steady on slow demand.

text.p: French wheat, barley and maize prices were steady amid dreary export prospects, dealers said on Tuesday.
Wheat lacked direction and business was thin, with buyers and sellers focussed on different delivery periods, they said.
"There is no possible match", one said.
Rouen wheat for February was paid at 825.50 francs per tonne at public silos and March wheat was bid at 845-847.50 francs per tonne, unchanged on Monday.
Barley at Dunkirk, the main outlet for exports to Saudi Arabia, was bid at 860 francs per tonne and offered at 870 francs, unchanged on Monday.
Dealers cited market rumours that one ship was expected very shortly in Dunkirk to load barley for Saudi Arabia. But freight sources would not confirm it.
Bordeaux-delivered maize was bid at 835 francs for February-March, unchanged from Monday.
French grain prices exclude domestic carrying charges of 3.64 francs per tonne, which must be added to every half-month between August 1 last year and the delivery period in question.
May Fob barge Matif wheat futures were bid at 884 francs per tonne and offered 890 francs per tonne but there was no trade.
